contracts.commit_point: Atomic temp-file write plus temp_path.replace(full_path): apply_edit exact path (editor.py 561-565), _apply_llm_edit (editor.py 461-463), write_approved_edit (editor.py 657-659), and the verify_and_rollback restore write_text (editor.py 745).
contracts.declared_mechanism: _resolve_target_path builds the target (repo-relative or absolute), resolves it, and requires it to fall under the resolved repo root, otherwise raising ValueError('Path traversal blocked: <file_path>'); every write entry point invokes it first (apply_edit, _apply_llm_edit, write_approved_edit, verify_and_rollback), and apply_edit/write_approved_edit convert the ValueError into a non-writing ok=False result.
contracts.forbidden_condition: A path-traversing write: an editor mutation whose file_path resolves outside the repo root, i.e., any target where full_path.resolve() is not relative to Path(repo_path).resolve().
pending_binding_information: Whether any agent tool, lifecycle hook, or agent-generated input other than apply_fix reaches write_approved_edit or verify_and_rollback (the only supplied caller is the POST /review/apply-edits handler at main.py 1194-1237).
contracts.protected_operation: Editor disk writes: apply_edit's exact-replacement and LLM-as-editor writes, write_approved_edit's approved-content write, and verify_and_rollback's restore writes — each resolves its target through _resolve_target_path before touching the file; agent reach is established via apply_fix passing its tool-call file_path argument into apply_edit.
contracts.protected_resource: Files under the repository root (repo_path) — the filesystem containment boundary.
contracts.protection_obligation: Every disk write through the unified editor must resolve to a path inside the repo root: _resolve_target_path must reject any target whose resolved location escapes Path(repo_path).resolve() by raising 'Path traversal blocked' before any mutation occurs, at every write entry point (apply_edit, _apply_llm_edit, write_approved_edit, verify_and_rollback rollback writes).
scope_limits: Agent mediation is established only for the apply_fix tool path (apply_fix's file_path argument → apply_edit → _resolve_target_path); the same guard also protects non-agent HTTP review flows (POST /review/preview-edits dry-run via apply_edit; POST /review/apply-edits via write_approved_edit and verify_and_rollback), for which mediation is not established.
The guard rejects before mutation; the contract makes no claim about time-of-check-to-time-of-use between the resolve check and the later replace.
Coverage claims extend only to editor writes that route through _resolve_target_path; other filesystem writers in the repository are out of scope.

contracts.commit_point: Resumed execution of the write_tools node: tool.invoke('apply_fix') → apply_edit → temp-file write and temp_path.replace(full_path) committing the file mutation (atomic write in apply_edit's exact-replacement path).
contracts.declared_mechanism: Compile-time HITL guard: route_after_agent sends AI tool-call batches whose names intersect WRITE_TOOL_NAMES to the 'write_tools' node; compile_with_hitl(graph, interrupt_nodes=['write_tools']) compiles the builder with interrupt_before=['write_tools'] (plus SqliteSaver checkpointing), halting the graph before that node executes; /chat and /chat/stream surface the halt as interrupted=True/'interrupted' with proposed_action, and only POST /chat/approve resumes the checkpoint (action='approve' → graph.invoke(None)) or replaces the pending tool-call message and discards the action (action='reject').
contracts.forbidden_condition: Execution of the apply_fix write tool — and therefore the apply_edit disk mutation it performs — without prior human approval, i.e., any path where the write_tools node runs without a preceding /chat/approve action='approve' on the interrupted checkpoint (action='reject' must discard the pending action).
pending_binding_information: Implementation of state.get_agent()/state.require_index() (src/codewalk/api/state.py) is not in supplied views, so the wiring from /chat and /chat/approve to the compile_with_hitl-compiled graph is inferred from imports, docstrings, and proposed_write_action usage rather than directly evidenced.
Whether compile_with_hitl's async_checkpointer variant (_AsyncGraphContext, hitl.py 52-81, 105-106) is used by any production caller is not shown.

POST /voice/ask (main.py 1358-1367) invokes the same agent without checking graph_state.next; how a write_tools interrupt raised on a voice thread would be surfaced or approved is not established by supplied views.
contracts.protected_operation: Agent-initiated apply_fix tool invocation dispatched through the 'write_tools' graph node via tool.invoke, which calls apply_edit(repo_path, file_path, old_code, new_code) to rewrite repository files.
contracts.protected_resource: Repository files on disk under repo_path that apply_fix/apply_edit would overwrite.
contracts.protection_obligation: The agent's sole repo-mutating write tool apply_fix (WRITE_TOOL_NAMES = frozenset({'apply_fix'})) must not execute its body — the apply_edit call that mutates repository files on disk — until a human approves; the compiled graph must halt before the 'write_tools' node, and resumption or rejection may occur only through POST /chat/approve.
scope_limits: Interrupt scope is exactly WRITE_TOOL_NAMES = frozenset({'apply_fix'}); read-only tools route to read_tools and execute without interruption.
When an AI message mixes write and read tool calls, the read subset runs immediately and only still-pending write calls route back to write_tools via route_after_read/_pending_write_tool_calls.
The guard is graph-level (interrupt_before) plus API-level resume gating; apply_fix's own body contains no approval check.
This gate covers only the agent tool path; direct HTTP review writes (POST /review/apply-edits via write_approved_edit) are a separate non-agent write path outside this gate.
No judgment is made here about runtime effectiveness or bypass prevalence; the contract records only the declared registration and gating.

contracts.commit_point: Atomic temp-file write and temp_path.replace(full_path) in write_approved_edit (editor.py 657-659).
contracts.declared_mechanism: write_approved_edit re-reads the file after path containment and compares original_content != expected_original before any write; on mismatch it returns ok=False without mutating, and only on equality does it perform the temp-file/backup/replace write.
contracts.forbidden_condition: Overwriting a file whose current on-disk content differs from expected_original — the write is refused with 'File changed since preview — re-preview before applying' instead of committing.
pending_binding_information: No supplied evidence establishes agent mediation (agent tool, lifecycle hook, or agent-generated input) for write_approved_edit; confirm whether any agent path feeds edits or findings into POST /review/apply-edits.
contracts.protected_operation: write_approved_edit's atomic disk write of modified_content (invoked from POST /review/apply-edits with expected_original=edit.original_content).
contracts.protected_resource: Repository files under repo_path written by POST /review/apply-edits.
contracts.protection_obligation: write_approved_edit must refuse to commit a user-approved edit when the on-disk file no longer matches expected_original (the content the user previewed), preventing silent clobbering of changes made between preview and apply.
scope_limits: The check is exact whole-file string equality and guards only the preview→apply interval; it does not detect changes after the check.
expected_original is optional: when the caller omits it, the stale-preview refusal is skipped (editor.py 648).
Supplied source binds this operation only to the HTTP review flow; no agent tool or lifecycle wiring to write_approved_edit appears in the supplied views.
